summary: Preserved candidate c1723a1's experimental SageAttention integration and valid SM100 rejection. Reproduced the pinned dependency's missing comma, but not the review's claimed SM120 source-install rejection: SUPPORTED_ARCHS has no read sites, while setup.py and the public dispatcher contain explicit SM120 branches. Added documentation that SM120 remains hardware-unvalidated rather than speculatively rejecting it.

tests.what_was_measured: Ten focused adapter, input-rejection, ROCm/SM100 fail-closed, and server-argument admission regressions passed. The GPU numerical cases used an injected PyTorch SDPA callable, not SageAttention.
Eighteen tests and eighteen resolution-reproducibility subtests passed.
The malformed set evaluates to include 10.012.0, but SUPPORTED_ARCHS has one assignment and zero load sites. Separate active SM120 setup and dispatcher branches were present.
Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 used AMD Instinct MI355X; importing sageattention raised ModuleNotFoundError.

gpu_execution_evidence: The focused parametrized FP16/BF16 adapter tests ran on the assigned AMD Instinct MI355X. They executed PyTorch SDPA only; no SageAttention CUDA kernel ran.
remaining_limitations: No supported NVIDIA architecture or CUDA toolkit was available, so pinned SageAttention was not built or imported and no INT8 Q/K kernel executed.
The numerical adapter tests substitute full-precision PyTorch SDPA and do not establish quantized SageAttention accuracy.
No end-to-end serving, model-quality, long-context, throughput, latency, or memory result establishes the approximately 2x motivation.
Dense paged-KV gathering and materialized GQA/MQA expansion remain unbenchmarked and may offset kernel gains, especially for decode.

The pinned dependency's dead SUPPORTED_ARCHS declaration contains a missing comma. Because that declaration has no read sites, this investigation did not convert it into an unsupported-SM120 policy; an actual SM120 native build and execution remain unverified.
